attorneys.name: Howard B. Soypher
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Bethesda, MD
attorneys.bio:
Howard Soypher is an experienced litigator and family law attorney. In 2022, he was inducted as a Fellow into the American College of Trial Lawyers. Fellowship in the College is extended by invitation only and only after careful investigation, to those experienced trial lawyers of diverse backgrounds, who have mastered the art of advocacy and whose professional careers have been marked by the highest standards of professionalism, civility and congeniality. Membership in the College cannot exceed one percent of the total lawyers population of any state.

As an experienced litigator, Howard knows that it most often better for families to resolve their issues outside of a courtroom setting in an effort to better control their outcome, reduce animosity and reduce expenditure on legal fees. This experience allows Howard to carefully weigh settlement offers for his clients and help position them in determining the most efficient and probable path toward a successful outcome.

In addition to his family law practice, Howard has been representing clients in trusts and estate litigation for over 25 years. His practice includes will contests, pursuing rights on behalf of trust beneficiaries and representing trustees in the course of performing their duties.

Howard is the former President of the Maryland Chapter of the American College of Matrimonial Lawyers (AAML). The AAML is a national organization whose members are recognized for maintaining the highest degree of professionalism, integrity and excellence in the practice of family law.

Among the accomplishments that Howard is most proud of is the fact that many local lawyers have retained him to represent them in their own personal matters. Howard is frequently asked to speak at continuing educational seminars for other lawyers and judges on various family law topics, as well as various trial strategies and tactics. He enjoys doing so with the hope that some of his prior experiences will be of benefit to newer lawyers.

He is a frequent lecturer to various groups, including the Maryland Judiciary and family law attorneys on various aspects of family law.

Among the accolades that Howard has received was his being named Best Lawyer’s Washington D. C. Family Law “Lawyer of the Year” for 2021 and 2025.

attorneys.name: Michael L. Spekter
attorneys.practice_type: Federal Employment Law Including EEOC and MSPB Representation Lawyers in Silver Spring, MD
attorneys.bio:
Michael Spekter was of counsel to Gilbert Employment Law and specialized in representing federal employees in employment and retirement related matters. He practiced extensively before the U.S. Merit Systems Protection Board and the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, as well as both the local and federal Courts of the District of Columbia and Maryland, and especially at the Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, where he was responsible for a number of federal seminal retirement cases which protect the rights of part time federal employees.

He graduated from Villanova University, Bachelor of Arts cum laude, Honors Program, and received his Juris Doctor from Temple University Beasley School of Law, where he was a dean’s list student.

Prior to entering private practice, Mr. Spekter was one of the original senior prosecuting attorneys for the U.S. Office of Special Counsel, and litigated numerous seminal federal whistleblower retaliation and Hatch Act cases in the federal government. He has also successfully litigated numerous D.C. whistleblower cases.

In addition to practicing law, Mr. Spekter was an adjunct professor at both the University of Baltimore School of Law and American University Washington College of Law where he taught courses on Law Practice Management. He also coaches the ABA employment law moot court team from The University of Baltimore Law School.

He was also an active member of the Law Practice Division of the American Bar Association, where he held a position on the Leadership Council, and as an associate editor to Law Practice, the magazine of the Law Practice Division, where he was a regular contributor.

Mr. Spekter began his legal career in Arizona as a Pima County Public Defender, in Tucson, Arizona. He was a member of the bars of Arizona, Maryland and the District of Columbia, the companion federal courts and the U.S. Supreme Court.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Michael Spekter was of counsel to Gilbert Employment Law and specialized in representing federal employees in employment and retirement related matters. He practiced extensively before the U.S. Merit Systems Protection Board and the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, as well as both the local and federal Courts of the District of Columbia and Maryland, and especially at the Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, where he was responsible for a number of federal seminal retirement cases which protect the rights of part time federal employees.

He graduated from Villanova University, Bachelor of Arts cum laude, Honors Program, and received his Juris Doctor from Temple University Beasley School of Law, where he was a dean’s list student.

Prior to entering private practice, Mr. Spekter was one of the original senior prosecuting attorneys for the U.S. Office of Special Counsel, and litigated numerous seminal federal whistleblower retaliation and Hatch Act cases in the federal government. He has also successfully litigated numerous D.C. whistleblower cases.

In addition to practicing law, Mr. Spekter was an adjunct professor at both the University of Baltimore School of Law and American University Washington College of Law where he taught courses on Law Practice Management. He also coaches the ABA employment law moot court team from The University of Baltimore Law School.

He was also an active member of the Law Practice Division of the American Bar Association, where he held a position on the Leadership Council, and as an associate editor to Law Practice, the magazine of the Law Practice Division, where he was a regular contributor.

Mr. Spekter began his legal career in Arizona as a Pima County Public Defender, in Tucson, Arizona. He was a member of the bars of Arizona, Maryland and the District of Columbia, the companion federal courts and the U.S. Supreme Court.

attorneys.name: Robert Miles Stahl IV
attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices Robert M. Stahl LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Lutherville-Timonium, MD
attorneys.bio:
Robert M. Stahl, IV is the managing member of the Law Offices of Robert M. Stahl, LLC. He is both an attorney and a certified public accountant. He concentrates his practice on general business litigation, ranging from commercial disputes to bankruptcy. Also, his practice focuses on federal and state tax controversy, tax compliance, estate probate and administration, estate planning and estate litigation. He routinely provides representation on business formation and equity transactions, the negotiation and drafting of joint ventures, and the structuring and implementation of mergers and acquisitions. He counsels businessmen of all sizes in a variety of financial, transactional, employment and tax related matters. Mr. Stahl combines strategic thinking, attention to detail and drafting, and broad commercial experience to represent entrepreneurs, businesses and business owners knowledgeably, effectively, and successfully.

Mr. Stahl has more than 30 years of tax practice experience and provides counsel on a wide range of federal and state tax planning and compliance matters for individuals, tax-exempt organizations and business entities, including corporations, partnerships, limited liability companies and trusts. Mr. Stahl also has extensive experience in business related matters, such as acquisitions, asset purchases, choice of entity formation and corporate governance. He has experience in trials, arbitrations, mediations and administrative hearings in both federal and state court.

Mr. Stahl received his Juris Doctorate degree from the University of Baltimore School of Law and his Bachelor of Science in Accounting from The University of Baltimore in 1983 (magna cum laude). He had previously worked for the international accounting firm of Deloitte & Touche from 1983 to 1984, where he practiced in the audit department.

Mr. Stahl is admitted to practice law in Maryland and before the United States District Court of Maryland, the United States Bankruptcy Court and the United States Tax Court. He serves on the board of directors of both private and publicly held companies and has acted as a significant resource to those companies in that capacity. Mr. Stahl was elected to the board of directors of the Slavie Federal Savings Bank in 2002 where he serves as the chairman of the Audit Committee and the chairman of the Trouble Loan Workout Committee. In addition, he routinely attends various banking and financial institution seminars, including the annual Rowles & Company Independent Community Bank Conference, the annual Directors Institute Conference sponsored by the Pennsylvania Banker’s Association, the annual Parente Beard Financial Institutions Seminar, and various other FDIC sponsored conferences. Mr. Stahl is a member of numerous professional associations including the Maryland State Bar Association, the Maryland Trial Lawyers Association, the American Association of Attorney-Certified Public Accountants, the National Association of Consumer Bankruptcy Attorneys and the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

attorneys.name: Rue P. Stewart Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Custody Lawyers in Towson, MD
attorneys.bio:
I've been working with families ever since I started practicing law in January of 2006. My first job as an attorney was as a Family Advocate Attorney for five years at an agency called East Baltimore Development, Inc. When I formed the Stewart Law Office in 2011, I soon became attracted to assisting clients in their divorces. I then made it the primary focus of the firm.

I feel honored to have the privilege of being a divorce attorney because of my own personal experiences. I know from my own life, I've been able to go through some difficult challenges, but I've been able to realize that inside of those, they were great opportunities that have been adapted into my practice. My faith has grown deeply regarding these challenging experiences and has refined my life in many ways.

While being a 5th year Sophomore in College on academic probation and being involved in a serious car accident, great appreciation during these challenges was obtained.

I have realized in my own life, when I became brave enough to walk through these struggles, I was then able to find the blessings inside of my own challenges.

Blessings and accomplishments to date: I have been married to my wife for almost 20 years. I have published my book in reference to my struggles and the blessings along the way. I was able to go back to school, graduate and then attend law school. I have a successful law practice and am now also attending Harvard University Extension School which has been a dream of mine. I am currently on my 6th class with a standing 3.6 grade point average. Through my challenges in life, these wonderful experiences took place.

I know how difficult it can be to even begin to lean into the fear of these problems that are right in front of us. It can take so much courage and faith just to decide to move forward, to even take that first step; especially for the client who has been paralyzed by the dilemma of their marriage and custody problems but knows with all their being that they somehow need to move forward.

Here at the Stewart Law Office, we provide empathy, hope, strength and legal counsel to our clients in assisting them in walking through one of the most difficult challenges in their lives while supporting them to look for the blessings inside of their difficulties.

attorneys.name: Vaughn Stewart
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Lutherville-Timonium, MD
attorneys.bio:
Vaughn Stewart focuses his practice on consumer protection and tenants’ rights, with a particular emphasis on holding powerful institutions accountable when they take advantage of vulnerable communities. He represents individuals and classes of consumers in cases involving:

Tenant protections, including challenges to unlawful or deceptive rental charges and junk fees, as well as suits against tenant screening companies for inaccuracies in tenant reports.

Elder fraud and scams, pursuing claims against financial institutions and cryptocurrency platforms that fail to safeguard seniors from fraud.

Debt collection abuses, such as aggressive or unlawful debt collection tactics and attempts to recover money not actually owed.

Landlord habitability violations, including claims for failure to address unsafe living conditions such as pest infestations.

Credit reporting violations, litigating against major credit reporting agencies for inaccuracies and inadequate investigations under the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA).

Before joining Santoni, Vocci & Ortega, LLC, Vaughn practiced law at a large firm in Washington, D.C., and at a small firm in Maryland. He began his legal career as a law clerk for Judge John T. Nixon of the United States District Court for the Middle District of Tennessee.

In addition to his legal practice, Vaughn represents District 19 in the Maryland House of Delegates, where he has become one of the legislature’s leading champions for housing justice and economic fairness. He currently serves as Chief Deputy Majority Whip and as Chairman of the Motor Vehicle and Transportation Subcommittee. In 2023, he was recognized as the Housing Advocate of the Year by Economic Action Maryland.

Vaughn graduated magna cum laude from the University of Pennsylvania and cum laude from New York University School of Law, where he served as an editor of the NYU Law Review. He lives with his family in Rockville.

attorneys.name: Sean E. Suhar
attorneys.practice_type: Community Association Law Lawyers in Columbia, MD
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Suhar practiced law in Maryland for almost 10 years exclusively in the area of community association law. He has developed extensive experience in providing general legal representation and debt collection services for condominiums and homeowners associations across the State of Maryland. This experience includes debt collection, covenants enforcement, bankruptcy, foreclosure, corporate law, fair housing laws and civil litigation. Mr. Suhar specializes in providing community associations with a review and analysis of their governing documents, relevant statutes, and case law necessary for the association's efficient operation and for keeping property values high.

Mr. Suhar is able to provide a full range of legal services to condominiums and homeowners associations. He handles advising communities regarding compliance with laws governing non-stock corporations, and concerning compliance with local, state and federal statutes. This experience is combined with problem solving skills and a practical approach to helping Boards of Directors and Community Managers deal with the challenges which face community associations today.

Mr. Suhar has practiced regularly in both the District and Circuit Courts of Maryland. He has successfully handled numerous covenants enforcement cases in the Circuit Court, and has argued in the Maryland Court of Special Appeals.

Mr. Suhar is a native of Cincinnati, Ohio. He is a 1994 graduate of the University of Cincinnati, having earned a Bachelor's in Urban Planning. In 2002, Mr. Suhar graduated from the University of Dayton, School of Law. While in law school, Mr. Suhar competed on the Bankruptcy Moot Court Team, which traveled to New York. He also served indigent clients as part of the University's Law Clinic. Mr. Suhar was also a member of the Phi Alpha Delta Law Fraternity.

Since December, 2002, Mr. Suhar has been admitted to practice law in the State of Maryland. He is also a member of the Maryland State Bar Association, the Anne Arundel County Bar Association, and a past member of The James C. Cawood Jr. American Inns of Court which is based in Annapolis.

Prior to attending law school, Sean worked as a city and regional planner for local and regional planning agencies providing various services to government officials in the areas of transportation and economic development.

Mr. Suhar brings to Nagle & Zaller the values of hard work, commitment, and integrity. He also exhibits these ideals in his personal life. He is a devoted husband and father to his wife April, and their three children. Mr. Suhar has dedicated much of his life to the Boy Scouts of America, having attained the rank of Eagle Scout, and having served as a Boy Scout and Cub Scout leader. Sean enjoys spending time with his family, being an active member of his Church community, supporting local sports teams, and camping among other outdoor activities.

attorneys.name: Deryn A. Sumner
attorneys.practice_type: Federal Sector Employment Discrimination Lawyers in Silver Spring, MD
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Deryn A. Sumner is the Managing Partner of Gilbert Employment Law, as well as Co-Chair of the firm's Federal Sector EEOC Practice Group. She focuses her practice on representing federal employees and agencies before the EEOC and has worked on hundreds of cases involving claims of employment discrimination on the basis of disability, race, age, religion, retaliation and other bases. Ms. Sumner also has experience representing employees and agencies in cases of whistleblower retaliation and adverse action challenges before the MSPB.

Ms. Sumner graduated from American University's Washington College of Law in Washington, D.C. While in law school, she served as a note and comment editor on the Administrative Law Review, as well as co-chair of the Labor and Employment Law Society. Ms. Sumner also holds a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from the University of Southern California in Los Angeles, California.

Ms. Sumner is the co-author of several books on federal sector employment law including Representing Agencies and Complainants Before the EEOC; Federal Sector Disability Discrimination Law Desk book; Compensatory Damages and Other Remedies in Federal Sector Employment and Discrimination Cases; EEO Counselors' and Investigators' Manual; and an annual Consolidated Federal Sector EEO Update. Ms. Sumner was previously an instructor with the Federal Employment Law Training Group (FELTG) and now provides training with Gilbert Training Group in coordination in cyber FEDS® to agency representatives, EEO counselors and investigators, and reasonable accommodation coordinators.

attorneys.name: Heather R. Sweren
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Gaithersburg, MD
attorneys.bio:
Heather R. Sweren joined the firm as an Associate in 2006 and was promoted to Partner in 2015. She is licensed to practice law in Maryland. Ms. Sweren received her Bachelor of Science degree from the University of Maryland, College Park, in 2001 and her Juris Doctorate from the University of Baltimore School of Law in 2005.

Ms. Sweren is actively involved in several Maryland Bar Association committees and organizations, and previously served as a co-chair to the Montgomery County Bar Association Family Law Section for 2 years. She is the liaison to the Montgomery County Bar Association, Family Law Section for the Women's Commission of Montgomery County. In this role she helps coordinate the Commission's efforts to educate women on the divorce and family law process. Ms. Sweren is also a member of the Montgomery County Bar Association Judicial Selections Committee, the Montgomery County Inns of Court, Montgomery County Women's Bar Association, and the Peer Review Committee for the Attorney Grievance Commission of Maryland.

Ms. Sweren assists annually in the preparation of The Family Law Update, which summarizes new legislation and reported case law in the previous 18 months. She presents these materials for both the Maryland State Bar Association and Montgomery County Bar Association each year.

Prior to her employment with the firm, Ms. Sweren interned with the Honorable Gary Everngam in the District Court for Montgomery County, Maryland, and the Honorable John W. Debelius, III, in the Circuit Court for Montgomery County, Maryland. She then clerked with the Honorable William J. Rowan, III, in the Circuit Court for Montgomery County, Maryland.

attorneys.name: Florian Tabaku Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Law Lawyers in Rockville, MD
attorneys.bio:
Florian Tabaku’s path to becoming a dedicated advocate for families began at Mount St. Mary’s University, where he earned his Bachelor of Arts degree. Armed with a clear vision and the drive to pursue it, he then set his sights on Thomas M. Cooley Law School, fueled by a passion for family law.

Driven by the desire to help families navigate the complexities of legal matters, Florian focused his practice on domestic relations across the state of Maryland. He channels his passion, determination, and strategic thinking into crafting winning solutions for his clients, time and again.

His commitment to serving the community was evident even during his law school days. Florian volunteered at the Sixty Plus Elder Law Clinic, aiding vulnerable individuals who might not otherwise have access to legal representation. From crafting simple estate planning documents to tackling intricate litigation, his dedication earned him the esteemed Board of Directors’ Award for Outstanding Lawyering.

Florian’s exceptional skills and dedication have solidified his reputation as an accomplished and trusted attorney. He prioritizes personalized attention, meticulously guiding clients through life-altering legal challenges in a cost-effective and efficient manner. Beyond legal expertise, he embodies the quintessential advocate – dedicated, hardworking, thorough, and tough.

His clients consistently entrust him to deliver professional, responsive, and proactive representation. He serves as a reliable pillar of support, navigating through legal complexities with clarity and unwavering commitment.

attorneys.name: Eden O. Terenzini
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Rockville, MD
attorneys.bio:
A trained litigator, mediator, negotiator and collaborative law practitioner, Ms. Terenzini is experienced in all facets of family law. Her practice includes assisting clients to reach resolution in matters related to divorce, property distribution, business valuation, alimony, and retirement asset division. She also represents fathers, mothers, children and other involved relatives in custody, visitation, access, child support and paternity proceedings. In addition, Ms. Terenzini’s experience includes litigation and administration of adult guardianship cases, as well as administration of estates and trusts.

Ms. Terenzini has repeatedly been named by Maryland Super Lawyers publications as a “Rising Star” in family law. She also has twice received the Women’s Bar Association of Maryland’s President’s Award for Outstanding Member.

Ms. Terenzini serves on the executive boards of the Association of Family and Conciliation Courts (Maryland Chapter) and the Women’s Bar Association of Maryland Inc. She also serves as co-chair of the Judicial Selections Committee of the Women’s Bar Association of Maryland and is a member of the family law sections of the American Bar Association, the Maryland State Bar Association and the Bar Association of Montgomery County. Ms. Terenzini volunteers her time at the Montgomery County Bar Foundation’s Pro Bono Legal Advice Clinics.

A cum laude graduate of Heidelberg College (now University), in Ohio, Ms. Terenzini earned a bachelor’s degree in English and philosophy. She also holds a master’s degree in English from the University of Rochester. Ms. Terenzini received her law degree from the University of Maryland School of Law, where she was editor of the Notes and Comments section of the Journal of Race, Religion, Gender and Class.

attorneys.bio:
Brian Thackston is a director of marketing and operations. Prior to joining a law firm, he spent 8 years helping to grow a digital marketing agency from 5 to 50+ people. His focus was spent on putting the right people and processes in the right places.

With marketing, Brian uses his legal knowledge to create impactful campaigns that put the right information in the right prospects' hands at the right time.

With operations, Brian focuses on optimizing the experience throughout the entire client journey -- from in-person events to web pages and ads, all the way through to reviewing successful client engagements, outcomes, and then re-engagements.

Brian holds a Bachelor of Arts degree in English Literature, which he received from the University of Maryland Baltimore County in 2010. He then received a J.D. from the University of Baltimore in 2016 after working through their part-time evening program.

Brian has taught digital marketing at technology incubators, universities (American University Kogod School of Business, Johns Hopkins Carey School of Business, Towson University, University of Baltimore). He also sits on Stevenson University Brown School of Business curriculum advisory board.

With operations, Brian focuses on optimizing the experience throughout the entire client journey -- from in-person events to web pages and ads, all the way through to reviewing successful client engagements, outcomes, and then re-engagements.

Brian holds a Bachelor of Arts degree in English Literature, which he received from the University of Maryland Baltimore County in 2010. He then received a J.D. from the University of Baltimore in 2016 after working through their part-time evening program.

Brian has taught digital marketing at technology incubators, universities (American University Kogod School of Business, Johns Hopkins Carey School of Business, Towson University, University of Baltimore). He also sits on Stevenson University Brown School of Business curriculum advisory board.

attorneys.name: Linda Hitt Thatcher
attorneys.practice_type: Management Lawyers in Greenbelt, MD
attorneys.bio:
An accomplished employment litigator and mediator, Linda has been consistently named one of "Washington's Top Employment Lawyers" by Washingtonian Magazine since 2007 and was named to the Washingtonian “Top Lawyers Hall of Fame” honor roll—their coveted lifetime achievement award—in 2022. Linda was also named to The Daily Record’s “2023 Employment Law Power List” as a top “Maryland Power Player” and among “the most influential and respected practitioners in the employment law sector in Maryland.”

Linda has earned accolades from judges, peers, and clients. A grateful client said of her: “Linda’s legal acumen, years of experience, and deep understanding of human nature combine to make her an effective advocate. She is equal parts grit and compassion, a great listener who cuts to the heart of the matter, and she was ALWAYS available to me.” Another client wrote that “Linda is—quite literally—the best in the business. If you’re looking for the very best to fight for you—no matter how complicated the issue might be, Linda and her team are the only option.”

Her practice includes all aspects of employment law, including corporate counseling, EEO training, and litigation on behalf of employers and employees. She has appeared on NBC and Working Women television.

Linda successfully represented women golfers at many of the Maryland Golf and Country Clubs. Her efforts resulted in changes to voting, membership, and golfing rules so that women and men golfers are now treated equally. Linda's accomplishments are documented in the book: “The Unplayable Lie: The Untold Story of Women and Discrimination in American Golf.”

In 2023, Linda was honored to be appointed to the Board of Directors for “Swinging With Purpose.” SWP is a 501c3 organization that holds event-based fundraisers to provide support to grassroots organizations serving the needs of women, girls, and children in communities across the United States. Since their inception in 2013, SWP has raised and distributed over $1,200,000.00 to countless organizations that assist women in need.

Linda has served as a faculty member for the National Institute for the Trial Advocacy (NITA) Skills Program at Georgetown University Law Center, and she is a frequent panel member and speaker for numerous CLE programs and conferences. She served as co-counsel with the Washington Lawyers Committee for Civil Rights and Urban Affairs in employment discrimination cases.

Linda is a permanent member of the Fourth Circuit Judicial Conference, a past President of the Board of Governors of the Federal Bar Association of Maryland, and an active member in the Women's Bar Associations of both Maryland and the District of Columbia.

Linda attended Longwood University in Virginia on a full gymnastic scholarship. She is a graduate of St. Mary's University Law School, San Antonio, Texas, where she served as an associate editor of the Law Review.

In her spare time, Linda is an avid golfer and swimmer. She also loves to paint and listen to classical music. She has two adult sons (J. Michael and Luke) and a granddaughter, Nora James, who along with her husband, are the joy of her life.

attorneys.name: Katie Thomas
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Columbia, MD
attorneys.bio:
Katie focuses her practice in the areas of estate planning, special education law, and guardianships. Prior to joining Ally Legal Planning, Katie previously worked in family law for many years and developed a reputation for personalizing her representation for each client and zealously advocating for her clients through negotiations and litigation. As part of her family law background she is well versed in the nuances of pre and post-nuptial agreements. Katie is also a mediator and uses her experience to facilitate settlements.

Katie takes time to get to know each client and works with them to determine the best path forward and implement the plan based on their unique circumstances. She regularly helps clients obtain guardianship of the person or property for a loved one, attends IEP or 504 meetings with parents, and helps families create an estate plan that is appropriate for their individual needs.

Katie has been a guest speaker at countless Baltimore-Washington events about raising a child with disabilities and complex medical needs. Outside of work, she volunteers her time as a board member for Liver Mommas, Inc. and regularly fosters and trains dogs for a local animal rescue.

Katie is a Maryland native and lives in Montgomery County with her husband, two children, and two dogs.

attorneys.name: Jiexi Tian
attorneys.practice_type: Sexual Abuse Lawyers in Baltimore, MD
attorneys.bio:
Jiexi Tian is an attorney with a relentless drive to go the extra mile for her clients. With a sincere dedication to clients’ well-being, she brings a unique blend of ambition and empathy to her practice. Jiexi’s legal journey has been marked by a commitment to advocacy and service, previously within the realms of family law and employment discrimination, and now making a difference as part of the Sexual Abuse team at Janet, Janet & Suggs.

Prior to joining Janet, Janet & Suggs, Jiexi’s professional focus was on family law, where she handled a diverse array of cases, including divorce, custody disputes, domestic violence matters, and child abuse and neglect issues involving child protective services. Her experience extends beyond family law, having been exposed to a broad spectrum of legal matters while working at different firms. This exposure encompassed personal injury claims, medical malpractice suits, tort cases, employment disputes, and criminal defense.

During law school, Jiexi actively engaged in clinical work, serving as a student attorney and advocating for victims of crimes, individuals struggling with mental health disorders, and those seeking post-conviction relief. Her academic journey includes graduating from UCLA with a major in Psychology before earning her Juris Doctor from the University of Maryland Francis King Carey School of Law.

Jiexi is bilingual in English and Mandarin Chinese, enabling her to effectively serve a diverse clientele. By embracing cultural differences and approaching each case with mindfulness and sensitivity, Jiexi strives to provide legal representation that is not only linguistically accessible but also culturally competent.

Outside of her legal endeavors, Jiexi has a deep love for animals. She volunteers at local shelters and aspires to one day rescue and provide a loving home for stray, abandoned, and abused animals.

With her diverse background, unwavering dedication, and heartfelt compassion, Jiexi is ready to provide exceptional legal representation and support to her clients in their time of need.

attorneys.name: Kevin M. Tracy
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Counseling & Dispute Resolution Lawyers in Annapolis, MD
attorneys.bio:
Kevin possesses a calming nature that assists him in effectively analyzing and approaching all of his clients’ legal concerns. He has extensive experience in construction and real estate development, as well as land use and zoning, business disputes and litigation. In dealing with a variety of legal issues, Kevin strives to get to the heart of any issue quickly to focus on an efficient yet cost effective resolution for his clients. He recognizes and analyses the economics of each issue to tailor an individual approach to create an end result that provides value to the client. Kevin says that the best piece of advice he has ever received is to “be persistent, honest and respectful,” and he exemplifies all of these traits admirably.

Kevin acts as corporate council to general contractors, subcontractors, builders and other businesses in a variety of industries. He can do it all, from contract review, drafting and negotiations; resolving payment disputes or mechanic’s lien claims; to mediating, arbitrating, or litigating construction disputes in both federal and state courts.

Mr. Tracy serves as a Director, Secretary and general county for the Associated Builders & Contractors - Chesapeake Shores Chapter, Inc. He received the ABC Chesapeake Shores Excellence in Construction Award for the design and construction of his energy efficient, solar tempered home on the Eastern Shore.

As McNamee Hosea’s most musically talented attorney, Kevin minored in music in college and plays the piano. He also enjoys spending time with his family and friends while cruising the Chesapeake Bay.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Severn, MD
attorneys.bio:
Rebecca S. Trevillian graduated from George Mason University School of Law in 2004, was admitted to practice law in the State of Maryland in December 2004, and has 18 years of experience related to family law cases. After her graduation from law school, she clerked for the Honorable Karen H. Abrams on the St. Mary’s County Circuit Court from August 2004 through August 2006. During her clerkship, Rebecca was exposed to many types of cases, but the majority of her time was spent focusing on assisting Judge Abrams in rendering decisions in divorce, child custody, child visitation, property, and child support cases.

Rebecca was a senior associate in an Annapolis law firm from August 2006 through July 2014, where her concentration was family law, including custody, divorce, visitation, child support, contempt, modification, separation agreement, prenuptial agreements, as well as protective orders. Rebecca is certified to mediate custody, visitation, child support, property, and alimony issues, and can provide mediation services for individuals as a cost-effective alternative to litigation.

Rebecca is a member of the Anne Arundel County Bar Association, Maryland State Bar Association, Howard County Bar Association, as well as a Court Approved Custody, Visitation, and Property division Mediator for Anne Arundel and Howard County.

attorneys.name: John E. Tsikerdanos
attorneys.practice_type: Collections Lawyers in Columbia, MD
attorneys.bio:
John E. Tsikerdanos has been practicing law in Maryland and the District of Columbia for over eight years. Upon graduating from the West Virginia University College of Law in 2008, John has worked as an associate at law firms located in Maryland and D.C. Initially, John's practice was concentrated on creditors' rights and bankruptcy, as he represented both debtors and creditors throughout the bankruptcy process. In addition to his creditors' rights and bankruptcy practice, John began representing community associations throughout Maryland and D.C. He has represented community associations, as well as provided counsel to management companies and board of directors of community associations, advising them on issues related to collections, covenant enforcement and construction defects. His experiences include drafting of governing document amendments, board resolutions, and rules and regulations, as well as representation of community associations throughout the entire collection process. John is a member of the Maryland State Bar Association, Montgomery County Bar Association, Frederick County Bar Association, and the District of Columbia Bar Association. John lives in Frederick County with his wife, daughter and son, and he enjoys spending time with his family and being involved in sports.

attorneys.name: James P. Ulwick
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Baltimore, MD
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Ulwick became a principal of the Firm in 1986. His practice is wide-ranging, including criminal and civil litigation of all kinds.

During law school, Mr. Ulwick served as an associate editor of the Catholic University Law Review. Following his clerkship, he spent six years as a federal prosecutor; three years as an Assistant United States Attorney for the District of New Jersey (1978-1981), and three years as an Assistant United States Attorney for the District of Maryland (1981-1984).

During his years as an Assistant U.S. Attorney, Mr. Ulwick tried numerous cases, including prosecution of labor racketeering, political corruption, and other violations of federal law. Since joining the Firm, Mr. Ulwick has tried many cases in state and federal courts, including: banking, criminal defense, class actions, contracts, personal injury, legal and medical malpractice, RICO, construction, equal employment, real estate, securities, toxic tort, and other cases.

Mr. Ulwick is a Fellow in the American College of Trial Lawyers, and a permanent member of the Judicial Conference for the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit. He has been listed for more than 15 years in the publication, The Best Lawyers in America (three categories: Commercial Litigation, White-Collar Criminal Defense, and Bet-the-Company Litigation). Chambers USA rated Mr. Ulwick as one of the best commercial litigators in Maryland for 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, and 2011. Chambers lists Mr. Ulwick, with only six other lawyers, in Band 1 of leading individuals in litigation. Mr. Ulwick is listed in Maryland Super Lawyers 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010 and 2011, most of those years as one of the State's top 50 attorneys

attorneys.name: Prudence Avery Upton
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Rockville, MD
attorneys.bio:
Family law involves guiding families through their most difficult times -- divorce, custody disputes, support issues. I do my best to get my clients through doing the least damage possible to the family relationships. In many cases this results in some sort of agreement between the parties to resolve their dispute. Sometimes, however, it is necessary to take the case through the court system to have a judge decide. When that happens I bring my litigative skills to bear.

I am frequently appointed to be a Best Interest Attorney by the court to represent children in custody cases. These cases are already contentious; otherwise the court would not appoint me. When my clients are the children I make my own determination as to what is in their best interests and bring that to the court for the judge to consider in making the final decision.

Whether my client is the children or one of the adults, I look for ways to help them come to the best outcome, be it agreement or court judgment.

attorneys.bio:
A principal in Joseph, Greenwald & Laake's Civil Litigation and Criminal Defense practice groups, Steven Vinick has more than 20 years of experience in representing clients in matters including medical malpractice, personal injury and criminal defense. Over the course of that career, Steven has earned a reputation as a skilled litigator and highly effective courtroom advocate.

Steven has obtained numerous significant verdicts on behalf of his clients, including an $11.5-million verdict for a client whose father was shot and killed by police officers. Steven's reputation as a fearsome courtroom opponent who obtains excellent results helps him negotiate favorable settlements on behalf of his clients. He takes pride in the fact that he receives many referrals from other attorneys and former clients, all of whom respect his legal acumen, his honesty and his empathy for his clients.

Steven was named Trial Lawyer of the Year by the Maryland Association for Justice, and has been named a Maryland SuperLawyer each year from 2011 to the present. He is a frequent lecturer on topics including civil litigation, automobile claims, depositions, Medicare and criminal defense for the National Business Institute and Maryland State Bar Association.

Outside of work, Steven enjoys skiing and running, and spending time with his three daughters and his wife.

attorneys.name: Shawn Vinson Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Severna Park, MD
attorneys.bio:
Shawn Vinson brings a diverse and highly respected background in estate matters and civil litigation to the firm. He has extensive experience handling a wide range of estate-related issues as well as complex civil litigation, and has appeared before the Appellate Court of Maryland and numerous trial courts throughout the State.

Prior to joining the firm, Mr. Vinson served as an Assistant State’s Attorney, where he gained significant courtroom experience and a deep understanding of Maryland law. His litigation background also includes matters involving asbestos, lead paint, and personal injury claims. In addition, he has handled forfeiture and replevin actions and cases arising under the Maryland Public Information Act.

Mr. Vinson is a retired law enforcement officer, a role that provided him with a strong foundation in public service, investigative work, and client advocacy. His professional experience further includes work with the public school system and government relations involving the Maryland State Legislature, giving him valuable insight into the intersection of law, policy, and community interests.

He is an active member of the Maryland Bar and remains deeply committed to professional and community service. Mr. Vinson serves on the Calvert Hall College High School Board of Trustees and is a Board Member and Secretary of the Family Crisis Center of Baltimore County. He is also a member of FOP Lodge #4, the Harford County Association of Realtors, and the Peer Review Committee of the Maryland Attorney Grievance Commission. He previously volunteered as an attorney with the Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service.

Mr. Vinson’s broad legal experience, public service background, and commitment to the community make him a valuable asset to both the firm and the clients he serves.

attorneys.practice_type: Tenants' Rights Lawyers in Lutherville-Timonium, MD
attorneys.bio:
Matthew Thomas Vocci is a partner in the law firm of Santoni, Vocci & Ortega, LLC. He represents and advocates on behalf of low-income Marylanders and strives to provide high-quality legal representation for those who would otherwise not be able to afford an attorney. If there are landlords, property managers, lenders, debt collectors, employers, bail bondsman that are taking advantage of regular folks, Matt and his firm work to bring them to justice. The majority of Matt's work relates in some way to housing. He represents tenants against landlords and property managers on a variety of cases such as consumer protection and consumer debt collection issues, habitability, Fair Housing Act violations, illegal evictions, and personal injuries. Matt has served as class counsel on several class actions, including a recent case that resolved favorably for tenants against a large, out-of-state property management company. He has also successfully represented those seeking wages/commissions from their employer or principal. He is a member of the MSBA’s Delivery of Legal Services Committee Council and the ACLU of Maryland Committee on Litigation and Legal Priorities. Matt also helps those injured in motor vehicle accidents, slip and falls, and dog bites.

Matt was an integral part of a trial team that represented a unit owner that suffered significant damages stemming from water infiltration and mold growth in a condominium unit. This case resulted in what is believed to be Maryland's largest judgment against a condominium board for failure to maintain and repair common elements resulting in damages to a single unit owner.

Matt is active in the community and is currently serving on the Committee on Litigation and Legal Priorities for the ACLU of Maryland. He is dedicated to the advancement of a civil and just society and has written for The Daily Record on topics involving those most vulnerable in our society. He has also published opinion pieces in The Baltimore Sun and Al Dia News.

Matt graduated cum laude from Temple University, Beasley School of Law in 2006 and served on the Editorial Board of the Temple Law Review.

attorneys.name: Erin K. Voss
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Columbia, MD
attorneys.bio:
Based in Columbia, Maryland, Erin K. Voss is a principal at Nagle & Zaller, P.C. Throughout her career, Ms. Voss has focused her practice on civil and personal injury litigation with an emphasis on negligence and motor vehicle accidents. She has substantial experience handling toxic tort cases, including property damage, groundwater contamination, environmental pollution, product liability and pharmaceuticals.

As a trial attorney, Ms. Voss has secured millions in damages on behalf of her personal injury clients. Notable victories include a $4 million compensation award in a groundwater contamination and property damage case and a $200,000 settlement in a medical malpractice case that did not cause permanent injury. In 2010, she was part of the trial team that won $34.3 million in damages for carbon monoxide poisoning suffered by her clients who were exposed while working at a downtown Baltimore restaurant. Before joining Nagle & Zaller, P.C., Ms. Voss was an associate at a well-known Baltimore litigation firm.

After graduating with a bachelor's degree in philosophy from Southern Illinois University in 2000, Ms. Voss went on to attend the University of Baltimore School of Law, where she was awarded her Juris Doctor in 2005. While in law school, she received an award for her charitable human rights work and was the captain of the American Association for Justice Student Trial Team, and she continues to participate in student trial teams and advocacy programs as an adjunct faculty member at her law school alma mater. Ms. Voss was also a student attorney with the Saul Ewing Civil Advocacy Clinic, where she represented clients who could not otherwise afford the services of a lawyer. She is admitted to practice in Maryland, Illinois and the District of Columbia.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Charles L. Waechter
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Lawyers in Baltimore, MD
attorneys.bio:
Baltimore Criminal Defense Law Firm

If you face criminal charges, an experienced and respected defense lawyer can help protect your rights, evaluate possible defenses, negotiate preferential plea bargains and use every facet of the law in your defense.

At the Law Offices of Charles L. Waechter, Attorney at Law, I have more than 40 years of experience defending people accused of all types of criminal charges, ranging from DWI and DUI to sex offenses and murder. I'm known as an aggressive and hard-hitting defense lawyer who will fight hard to keep your record as clean as possible and to minimize the effect of an arrest on your life.

With offices in Baltimore, Annapolis, Ocean City and Bel Air, I offer four convenient locations for people who are charged with crimes in Maryland.

No matter what kind of charges you face, I offer free initial consultation by phone or in one of my offices. If you are incarcerated, I can also meet with you in jail.

A Serious Lawyer for Serious Charges

I have the experience and knowledge to defend you against the most serious criminal charges such as Federal and State internet child pornography, sex offenses, DUI and DWI, drug offenses, solicitation and prostitution, assault and battery, and general traffic tickets, which can have a devastating effect on your life.

I will review the documents charging you with a crime, investigate the circumstances of your arrest and determine if any evidence should be suppressed. For example, if the police violated your Fourth Amendment constitutional rights against unreasonable search and seizure, I will seek to have the charges dismissed.

attorneys.name: Cristol Wagner
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning and Administration Lawyers in Annapolis, MD
attorneys.bio:
Cristol Wagner is an Associate Attorney at Sinclair Prosser Gasior, focusing on estate planning and estate administration clients. She initially joined the firm as a law clerk before being sworn in to practice law in Maryland, November 2023.

With both of her parents practicing law, Cristol always knew she would become an attorney. In law school, she assumed she would focus on international law but quickly realized she wanted to work in an area where she could see the impact of her work. After experiencing the stress and grief of her father’s passing, she wanted to gain the skills necessary to help others navigate similar experiences. Cristol’s kind, calm and attentive approach helps her support clients through developing secure estate plans or guiding families through the difficult estate administration process after losing a loved one.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

She is a member of the Maryland State Bar Association, the Women’s Bar Association of Maryland, the Anne Arundel County Bar Association and the American Academy of Estate Planning Attorneys. Cristol frequently advances her knowledge of estate planning laws and policies to provide clients with the most up-to-date information.

While in law school, she was a fellow in the Rose Zetzer Women, Leadership and Equality program, an editor of the Maryland Journal of International Law and a participant in the Fair Housing Clinic. Before joining Sinclair Prosser Gasior, she worked as a law clerk at a title company and another law firm, where she conducted research projects and gained insight into various legal topics.

EDUCATION

Bachelor of Arts in International Affairs and German Language & Literature, George Washington University, Magna Cum Laude

Juris Doctorate, University of Maryland Carey School of Law

Annually completes 36 continuing education credits required by the American Academy of Estate Planning Attorneys

PERSONAL

Originally from Harford County, Cristol has spent her entire life in Maryland. She currently lives in Crofton with her fiancé, Calvin. In her free time, she enjoys traveling, reading and spending time on the water.

attorneys.name: James D. Walsh
attorneys.practice_type: Estates and Trusts Lawyers in Columbia, MD
attorneys.bio:
James D. Walsh has been practicing law in Maryland for 35 years in the fields of estate planning, estate and trust administration, wills and probate, tax law, and business law. Jim is also a former certified public accountant for over 30 years, a background that allows him to bring a unique, tax-driven perspective to all his estate planning work. He frequently represents clients in tax controversies with IRS and state tax authorities in precedent-setting cases, such as Pfeufer v. Cyphers (Court of Appeals of Maryland 2007).

James D. Walsh has an AV Preeminent* rating under Martindale Hubbell’s peer review rating processTM, the highest possible rating that an attorney can receive from his or her peers. He is frequently in demand as a speaker on estate and tax issues for professional, legal, and accounting organizations, as well as community groups, and has served as an expert witness in both the Orphans’ and Circuit Courts.

He has also used his legal experience in the community by serving on the Howard County Board of Appeals, which is an appointed five-member citizen panel that hears appeals from the decisions of various Howard County government agencies. He is currently serving his second five-year term on the board, and has been elected chairperson three times by his fellow members of the panel. In 2011, he was a member of the Howard County Charter Review Commission, which is a 15-member citizen panel that reviews the Howard County Charter and makes recommendations for changes to the County Council.

Jim earned his B.S. and B.A. from John Carroll University in 1978 and his J.D. cum laude and Order of the Coif honors from University of Toledo College of Law in 1983. He was admitted to the Maryland State Bar in 1983 and the U.S. Tax Court Bar in 1984. Jim has spoken at several different events, including the Maryland Institute for Continuing Professional Education of Lawyers, Maryland State Bar Association, Maryland Association of Certified Public Accountants, National Business Institute, and the Association of Practicing Accountants. He is a member of several professional associations, including the Baltimore Estate Planning Council, Howard County Bar Association, Martindale-Hubbell Legal Directory, and Bar Foundation for Howard County. He has also chaired or co-chaired the Maryland State Bar Association, Maryland Certified Public Accountants, and the Howard County Board of Appeals.

attorneys.name: Cathleen F. Ward Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Glen Burnie, MD
attorneys.bio:
I founded this firm in 1997. At that time, I had a handful of clients and made quite a leap of faith by branching out on my own. However, I had a great mentor, Paul B. Rodbell, Esq., and truly helpful experience through earlier employment at two highly regarded Maryland law firms. When this firm first opened, I operated from a small office, sublet from a generous attorney and friend, J. Robb Cecil, Esq. Slowly and carefully, I built my practice and the firm. Today, we have a staff of 10 and moved in 2011 to our newly re-developed office building in the Glen Burnie Town Center.

I decided to become a lawyer while in high school and have been licensed to practice since 1990. I knew early on that the law was the right profession for me and I graduated from the University of Maryland – College Park with a degree in Law Enforcement. However, I wasn’t sure at the start of law school (University of Maryland at Baltimore, this time) what practice areas would be most interesting to me and, at the same time, best fit my skill set. During law school, I was truly blessed by working in the office of the General Counsel the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission under the supervision of the talented Honorable Patricia Mitchell. Here, I was able to work on the commission’s police force issues as well as on zoning and land use. The zoning experience at the commission paved the way to my next great experience working for a law firm in Prince George’s County where I expanded my zoning practice along with general business law and real estate transactions. I then became an associate at a law firm in Howard County, Maryland where I further expanded my zoning practice into Howard and Anne Arundel Counties and in more complex real estate transactions and financing, representing both lenders and borrowers for residential and commercial transactions.

Currently, I truly enjoy all manner of real estate and business cases often because I like solving the mathematical complexities presented by cases involving business matters and property issues. I joking call this area ‘math law’. I concentrate my practice in areas such as real estate, bankruptcy, financing, business transactions, zoning and contracts. Client success in these areas requires meticulous attention to detail and the innate ability to follow the numbers to the desired result. It is precisely these traits that I put to the service of our clients.

In my free time, I enjoy landscaping & gardening, running, scuba diving, skiing and, much to my husband’s dismay, re-designing our home (usually started by removing a wall, while he is at the store). My husband and I have three lovely children.

Here, I was able to work on the commission’s police force issues as well as on zoning and land use. The zoning experience at the commission paved the way to my next great experience working for a law firm in Prince George’s County where I expanded my zoning practice along with general business law and real estate transactions. I then became an associate at a law firm in Howard County, Maryland where I further expanded my zoning practice into Howard and Anne Arundel Counties and in more complex real estate transactions and financing, representing both lenders and borrowers for residential and commercial transactions.

Currently, I truly enjoy all manner of real estate and business cases often because I like solving the mathematical complexities presented by cases involving business matters and property issues. I joking call this area ‘math law’. I concentrate my practice in areas such as real estate, bankruptcy, financing, business transactions, zoning and contracts. Client success in these areas requires meticulous attention to detail and the innate ability to follow the numbers to the desired result. It is precisely these traits that I put to the service of our clients.

In my free time, I enjoy landscaping & gardening, running, scuba diving, skiing and, much to my husband’s dismay, re-designing our home (usually started by removing a wall, while he is at the store). My husband and I have three lovely children.

attorneys.name: Deborah L. Webb
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Bethesda, MD
attorneys.bio:
Deborah L. Webb is a divorce attorney practicing in Maryland and the District of Columbia for 30 years. She represents clients in all aspects of family law including negotiations leading to prenuptial and separation agreements and the litigation of issues related to the dissolution of marriage, child custody, child support, alimony, and equitable distribution of property.

Being a leader in the family law community is one of the main reasons that The Bar Association of Montgomery County named Deborah its “Family Law Practitioner of the Year” in 2015. Her colleagues often seek her assistance as a mediator to resolve complex family law cases. Deborah is a Fellow of the prestigious American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers (AAML), and International Academy of Family Lawyers having met their strict standards for admission.

Being detailed, organized and discreet are Deborah’s key attributes. She is strategic and creative in helping clients achieve their goals. Deborah has a wide breadth of experience in handling complex financial matters including executive compensation structures and business and stock option disputes between business owners and their spouses. She also has vast experience in representing clients in difficult custody matters involving addiction and relocation. Her clients include high net worth individuals, professional athletes, entrepreneurs and their spouses.

Having a criminal law background makes Deborah a skilled and strong advocate for her clients inside and outside of the courtroom. Getting the best negotiated settlement requires specialized advocacy and Deborah trained in negotiation techniques at the Program on Negotiation at Harvard Law School.

Divorce is highly personal. It affects every client, his or her children, and their financial future in their own unique way. Depending on the needs of the client, Deborah helps build a team of professionals to provide specialized advice, such as child custody experts, therapists, forensic accountants, investment advisors, tax and corporate counsel and estate planners to achieve the best outcome for her clients. Deborah excels at bringing cases to a resolution in an efficient and cost effective manner.

Deborah has served as a faculty member for continuing legal education courses sponsored by the AAML and Family Law Sections of the Maryland Bar, Montgomery County Bar and D.C. Bar.

Deborah has been listed among the top lawyers in The Washingtonian, Maryland Super Lawyers, District of Columbia Super Lawyers, Bethesda Magazine and Best Lawyers in America.

Her practice areas include Family Law, Collaborative Law, and Mediation and Arbitration Services.

attorneys.name: Thomas M. Weschler, Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Domestic Violence Lawyers in Frederick, MD
attorneys.bio:
Thomas M. Weschler, Jr. became an Associate at McLeod, Weschler & Yeager, P.C. in May 2009 and a Partner in January 2016. Tom was inspired to pursue a career in family law because of the personal experiences of close family members who underwent significant challenges in the family court system. Because of this, Tom strives to listen to all clients, to answer their questions, to help make them feel comfortable and to empower them throughout their cases. He does his very best to provide the compassion and attention each client needs, as he understands family law cases are highly charged emotionally and life-altering.

Tom handles domestic violence cases, complex separation and divorce cases, highly contested child custody and access disputes, alimony and child support cases, contempt and enforcement actions as well as drafts pre-nuptial and separation and property settlement agreements.

A parent himself, Tom has also obtained his certifications in order to represent children in custody dispute cases, and on numerous occasions, has been appointed by the Court to do so in many occasions in several jurisdictions.

Understanding that when parties are able to resolve their differences on their own, they are better able to craft an arrangement that better fits their needs and goals. Tom has been trained as a mediator and regularly attends mediation sessions with his clients. At these mediation sessions, he provides them with counsel, informing them of their rights and options, all in an effort to provide them with the necessary information in order to allow them to make the best decisions about their cases. Tom is also appointed by the Court to serve as a mediator for cases that involve issues related to custody, division of property and support.

From 2014-2022, Tom has been recognized as a Maryland Super Lawyer in Family Law. Tom is also a 2010 graduate of the Maryland State Bar Association's Leadership Development Program. He has received the distinguished David Hjortsberg Award (2014), has served on the Maryland State Bar Association's Board of Governors, and is a Fellow of the Maryland Bar Foundation. He currently sits on the executive committee of The Maryland Bar Foundation.

A well-rounded professional, Tom stays apprised of the latest changes to the law and how those changes can impact his clients. With his knowledge and experience, he has also been invited to present to other attorneys and mental health professionals about family law matters and the judicial process and has served as a mentor through the bar associations. With deep roots in Maryland, Tom gives back to the community through pro bono work and volunteer activities. He represents clients through the local county pro bono offices, has accepted cases through Maryland Volunteer Legal Services (MVLS) and has assisted at local pro se help desks.

attorneys.name: Janell F. Wheeler
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Bethesda, MD
attorneys.bio:
Janell Wheeler is an Associate Attorney at Hamelburg Law. She is committed to providing quality legal work to meet the individualized needs of our clients. Her practical experience with a variety of legal issues allows her to bring nuanced and insightful perspective to each client’s situation.

Janell practices in the areas of estate planning, probate and trust administration, business law, commercial and residential real estate, and litigation. Her ability to blend estate planning, business law, and real estate matters is particularly valuable in assisting our clients in crafting estate plans that include succession planning for their business as well as the transfer of real property.

Janell has earned a reputation as a skilled trusts and estates attorney, most recently being recognized as a 2024 Maryland Rising Star by Super Lawyers. She strives to simplify the estate planning process and creates unique plans to meet the different needs of each client. She is a compassionate partner to her clients, helping them to navigate the probate and trust administration process. When disputes occur between family members, Janell also litigates matters involving will contests and probate disputes

Janell also assists business owners with the many issues they face in owning and operating their business. She reviews and prepares employment agreements and business contracts, and assists in debt collection efforts. For her clients that own real estate, she drafts and reviews commercial leases and prepares deeds.

Janell graduated magna cum laude from American University Washington College of Law, where she served as Note and Comment Editor for American University Law Review. Recognizing the importance of community service, Janell regularly volunteers with various civic and religious organizations and local schools.

attorneys.name: Elizabeth A. Wilson
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Discrimination Lawyers in Silver Spring, MD
attorneys.bio:
Elizabeth A. Wilson is Counsel focusing on employment litigation in the private sector. Ms. Wilson holds a J.D. from Harvard Law School and a B.A. in English and Ph.D. in Comparative Literature and Literary Theory from the University of Pennsylvania.

Prior to joining Gilbert Employment Law, Ms. Wilson was an Associate in the Litigation department of Wilmer Cutler Pickering Hale and Dorr, where she was an integral part of the team that brought habeas corpus claims on behalf of war on terrorism detainees held in Guantanamo Bay culminating in the landmark Supreme Court case Boumediene v. Bush. She was also an Associate at Baach Robinson & Lewis (now Lewis Baach) where she represented released British Guantanamo detainees in claims for damages against the U.S. government (Rasul v. Myers) and brought the first habeas petitions on behalf of detainees in Bagram Air Force Base. She was the main drafter of a report on torture in Guantanamo Bay, published by the Center for Constitutional Rights. At WilmerHale and Lewis Baach, she also worked on corporate investigations and international litigation. During law school, she interned at the Public Corruption Unit of the Criminal Division of the US Attorney’s office in Boston and at Mintz Levin Cohn Ferris Glovsky and Popeo as a litigation associate.

Ms. Wilson then became assistant professor of international human rights law in the School of Diplomacy, Seton Hall University, where she focused on civil and political rights, including discrimination based on sex, race, and age.

Ms. Wilson has written extensively about the right to associate in the context of strikes and protest movements. She has been visiting professor at Columbia University’s Institute for Human Rights; Rutgers Law School, Newark, New Jersey; and the George Washington University Law School, Washington, DC. She has also taught as assistant professor in the Department of English, Yale University.

She is the recipient of a Fulbright scholarship, during which she taught at Johann Wolfgang Goethe University, Frankfurt am Main, Germany, and a Nehru-Fulbright Senior Scholarship, during which she did research on Gandhi’s legacy for the human rights movement at the Center for Policy Research in New Delhi, India. She has also received a German Academic Exchange Award (DAAD), during which she taught at Humboldt University, Berlin, Germany. She has also been a Senior Visiting Research Fellow at the Max Planck Institute for Contemporary Public Law and International Law in Heidelberg, Germany. She is the recipient of a grants from the ARCA Foundation and the International Center for Nonviolent Conflict for her work on nonviolent movements.

She is the author of People Power and International Human Rights: Creating a Legal Framework and numerous works on nonviolent resistance movements, human rights, and constitutional torts.

sections.content:
Elizabeth A. Wilson is Counsel focusing on employment litigation in the private sector. Ms. Wilson holds a J.D. from Harvard Law School and a B.A. in English and Ph.D. in Comparative Literature and Literary Theory from the University of Pennsylvania.

Prior to joining Gilbert Employment Law, Ms. Wilson was an Associate in the Litigation department of Wilmer Cutler Pickering Hale and Dorr, where she was an integral part of the team that brought habeas corpus claims on behalf of war on terrorism detainees held in Guantanamo Bay culminating in the landmark Supreme Court case Boumediene v. Bush. She was also an Associate at Baach Robinson & Lewis (now Lewis Baach) where she represented released British Guantanamo detainees in claims for damages against the U.S. government (Rasul v. Myers) and brought the first habeas petitions on behalf of detainees in Bagram Air Force Base. She was the main drafter of a report on torture in Guantanamo Bay, published by the Center for Constitutional Rights. At WilmerHale and Lewis Baach, she also worked on corporate investigations and international litigation. During law school, she interned at the Public Corruption Unit of the Criminal Division of the US Attorney’s office in Boston and at Mintz Levin Cohn Ferris Glovsky and Popeo as a litigation associate.

Ms. Wilson then became assistant professor of international human rights law in the School of Diplomacy, Seton Hall University, where she focused on civil and political rights, including discrimination based on sex, race, and age.

Ms. Wilson has written extensively about the right to associate in the context of strikes and protest movements. She has been visiting professor at Columbia University’s Institute for Human Rights; Rutgers Law School, Newark, New Jersey; and the George Washington University Law School, Washington, DC. She has also taught as assistant professor in the Department of English, Yale University.

She is the recipient of a Fulbright scholarship, during which she taught at Johann Wolfgang Goethe University, Frankfurt am Main, Germany, and a Nehru-Fulbright Senior Scholarship, during which she did research on Gandhi’s legacy for the human rights movement at the Center for Policy Research in New Delhi, India. She has also received a German Academic Exchange Award (DAAD), during which she taught at Humboldt University, Berlin, Germany. She has also been a Senior Visiting Research Fellow at the Max Planck Institute for Contemporary Public Law and International Law in Heidelberg, Germany. She is the recipient of a grants from the ARCA Foundation and the International Center for Nonviolent Conflict for her work on nonviolent movements.

She is the author of People Power and International Human Rights: Creating a Legal Framework and numerous works on nonviolent resistance movements, human rights, and constitutional torts.

attorneys.name: Lisa Roberts Windsor
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Glen Burnie, MD
attorneys.bio:
Lisa Roberts Windsor is a family law attorney and mediator with Zide Law Group, LLC. Lisa handles all matters related to family law, including divorce, custody, visitation, and support issues. Lisa is a strong advocate for clients throughout Maryland, and practices a client centered approach where each case is tailored to individual needs and goals. She recognizes that different cases require different approaches, and she carefully consults with each client in order to find workable solutions for clients. Lisa works hard to explore reasonable and favorable settlement options on behalf of her clients, and is known to her colleagues as a firm but reasonable negotiator. If a resolution cannot be reached, she is a confident and seasoned litigator who is a zealous advocate for her clients in the courtroom. Lisa also has an active mediation practice that includes both court ordered mediation and private mediation.

Lisa divides her time between the firm's eastern shore office in Cambridge and the Glen Burnie office. Lisa is a member of the Maryland State Bar Association and the Anne Arundel County Bar Association. She has been continuously recognized each year as a Rising Star by Maryland Super Lawyers since 2017. She resides on the mid-shore and is active in her local community.

attorneys.name: Beverly Winstead Esq
attorneys.practice_type: Tax Lawyers in Baltimore, MD
attorneys.bio:
Being an attorney has given Beverly Winstead the opportunity to change so many of her clients' lives for the better by solving their personal and business tax issues. From negotiating with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) a settlement that is comfortable for a client to getting IRS to release a lien or levy, the favorite part of her tax practice has always been the peace she gives to her clients when she tells them that their debt has been significantly reduced or their tax issues have been resolved.

Her decision to practice law was a natural fit because of her competitive spirit. She went to college on an athletic scholarship at Bowie State University (BSU) and received numerous honors, such as being selected to All-Conference, All- Regional, and All-Tournament teams during her tenure. To date she has been the only woman in the history of the Central Intercollegiate Athletic Association (CIAA) to win three championships.

She graduated from BSU with a degree in Business Administration with a concentration in finance. After finishing her undergraduate studies she worked for local government doing budgeting and teaching entrepreneurial skills. However, she was never satisfied with working for local government because she felt that she had a deeper calling. Her deep desire to help people sent her to the University of Maryland, School of Law. While at the University of Maryland she learned skills necessary to be an effective advocate.

Just as she did on the women's basketball team at Bowie State where she made CIAA history and was honored as the MVP of various tournaments, she always puts on a winner's attitude for her clients. She is excited to use her skills that she learned while playing sports, to be the MVP that resolves her client's problems.

Beverly is a member of the Maryland State Bar Association (MSBA), American Bar Association (ABA), the National Bar Association and the Fellowship of Christian Athletes (FCA) - Central Maryland. The Law Offices of Beverly Winstead, LLC is affiliated with the accounting firm, Winstead Tax Group, LLC.

Attorney Beverly Winstead also serves as the Clinical Law Instructor for the Low Income Taxpayer Clinic at the University of Maryland, School of Law.

attorneys.name: Wayne Wiseman
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Greenbelt, MD
attorneys.bio:
After graduating from Georgetown University Law Center in 1981, Wayne Wiseman maintained a successful and active practice handling a cross section of civil litigation, commercial and transactional matters, regulatory matters, and criminal defense trials and appeals. He was both the founding and managing partner of a highly successful Park Avenue law firm for twenty-two years, from 1987 until 2009. Wayne served as a faculty member of the National Institute of Trial Attorneys Trial Advocacy Skills Program at Georgetown University Law Center.

Wayne’s legal career began with employment as an Assistant District Attorney in New York City, where he tried over 30 jury trials to verdict, with a 97% conviction rate. After leaving the District Attorney’s Office, he built upon this trial experience by trying in excess of 100 cases to verdict in both the Federal and State court systems, covering a diverse range of subjects that included employment matters on behalf of both employers and employees, prosecuted and defended personal injury and medical malpractice cases, defended workers’ compensation cases, and defended clients against prosecution at the Federal and State levels. Wayne drew on his B.B.A. in accounting, economics and finance, along with his experience as a public accountant with a former “Big Eight” certified public accounting firm to advise clients on sensitive and complex financial matters, involving everything from corporate matters and structuring transactions to complex multi-million dollar forfeiture proceedings.

Of Wayne Wiseman, one grateful client said he is: “amazing, talented, and truly cares,” while another described him as “professional and informative with a refreshing approach.” After a lengthy trial, a business owner client said: “Wayne is a masterful trial attorney. The judge hung on his every word. I felt privileged to be represented by Wayne and the whole team.”

Wayne is an avid golfer and investor who enjoys spending time with his beloved wife, their dog, Max, friends and family.
